item.description:
Photos keep their own colour

Ferry used to fold an iPhone's HDR gain map back into the picture on the way out. On two thirds of photos that visibly changed the exposure — most often brighter, so faces washed out and lost detail — to reclaim a sliver of clipped highlight. Ferry now hands back the exposure the shot was metered for, the same rendition Photos exports.

The old behaviour is still there if you want it, and it now has a switch: Settings → HDR photos → Recover clipped highlights.

Photographs are checked before they're saved

Ferry has always measured its work on screenshots and logos, encoding a few versions and keeping the one that still looks right. Photographs skipped that check — they were saved at a fixed setting, sight unseen, and on more than half of them that setting was past the point Ferry would have accepted anywhere else. That's what made detail go soft and mushy.

Photographs now go through the same check as everything else. If the first attempt gives up too much, Ferry spends the bytes and tries again. Most photos are unaffected; the ones that were being quietly ruined come out visibly better, and a little larger.

You can keep every pixel

The resize setting only ever made images smaller, so on a photograph — already brought down to 2000px for the web — every size it offered did nothing at all. It now sets the size, in both directions, and there's an Original size option for keeping the full resolution.

Left alone, Ferry still brings photographs down to 2000px. That's where most of the saving comes from. If you had already picked a size in Settings, it now does what it says — which may mean larger files than you were getting.

Smaller files

Every AVIF Ferry wrote claimed to have transparency, even a photograph that plainly doesn't, and paid about 1% of its size to say so. Fixed.
